title: Opening the Club Riviera in 1944 as Earl Hines opens the Plantation
summary: After leaving in June 1944 they open the packed new black club, the Riviera, while Earl Hines with Sarah Vaughan opens at the Plantation.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What year did you leave the Club Plantation?

We left there in 1944. We finished in June of 1944. A week later, a week and a half later, we opened the Club Riviera, the same year. They opened up their first band -- their first band, I think, was Earl Hines. Earl Hines came in --

Yes. Earl Hines came in with Sarah Vaughan. Sarah Vaughan was a little girl that -- she was tiny, and she had on a little, funny-looking dress. She didn't know too much about stage presentation. But when she opened her mouth, you knew she was out there on the floor. Earl Hines'
band opened there. I think the next band was -- it might have been Noble Sissel or the Russell -- Louis Russell.
Louis Russell's band. In the meantime, we were opening, the Club Riviera was a new spot.
That was the new black spot.
That was the new black spot.

New black spot. And it was hot as fire there. I mean, that is, packed and jammed. We opened there with a big floor show. And the people fell in love with the Club Riviera. Opening night, the streets were just -- the whole entire block was just -- the policemen had to block the entire thing off. People were just lined up, trying to get in. Couldn't serve all the people.

In the meantime, at the Club Plantation, they were bringing in different acts -- Ella Fitzgerald, different ones. So finally, they just went broke paying those big prices. And those big acts, like Ella Fitzgerald. I mentioned Cab. I mentioned the Mills Brothers.
